This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 15.04.2023 at about 8.30 p.m. petitioner had been riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06- HP-7678 near Honnudike Hand Post,
Tumkuru-Kunigal Road, Guluru Hobli, Tumkur, at that time, a car bearing Reg.No.KA-06-MA-4697 driven the same at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, due to the said impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Government Hospital, Tumkuru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient, for which he has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 21 years, hale and healthy, doing agriculture and milk vending business, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.,

due to this accident he is not able to work,
he is under SCCH-5 complete bedrest and also suffering from permanent disability and lost his earning capacity.
Out of this accident crime No.73/2023 is registered against the driver of the said car before the Hebbur Police Station for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
R1 is the owner and R2 is insurer of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement.
He is entitled to take shelter under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further stated that, driver of the offending SCCH-5 vehicle does not possessed valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
He has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-06-MA-4697 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied age, occupation, income of the petitioner, occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained, treatment taken and expenses incurred by the petitioner towards injuries sustained by him.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:

2 ::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred SCCH-5 on 15.04.2023 at about 8.30 p.m. when petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No. KA-06-HP-7678 near Honnudike Hand Post, Tumkuru- Kunigal road, Guluru Hobli, at that time, Car bearing Reg.No.KA-06-MA- 4697 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW-1, examined Dr.B.Ramesh Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-2, Medical Record Department Incharge is examined as PW-3 and marked 17 documents as per Ex.P.1 to SCCH-5 Ex.P.17 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
: : REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:- In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of SCCH-5 spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of wound certificate is marked as Ex.P.6 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7.
9.
Further to substantiate the petitioner case, he examined one Doctor as PW-2 and medical record department incharge as PW-3.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 and his records those have marked i.e., as FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, IMV Report and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 15.04.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.

sentences.text: Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the SCCH-5 accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 15.04.2023 at about 8.30 p.m. when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-HP-7678 near Honnudike Hand Post, Tumkuru-Kunigal Road, Guluru Hobli,
Tumakur.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that,
petitioner has proved the SCCH-5 above issue No.1 in his favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained posterior dislocation of right hip, for which, he undergone treatment of closed reuction of dislocation.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9 issued by District Hospital, Tumkuru wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 15.04.2023 to 17.04.2023.

Further he has furnished OPD Bill of Rs.1,583/- marked as Ex.P.10 and CT-Scan films are marked as Ex.P.11.
13.
Ofcourse, PW-2 Dr.B.Ramesh, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital is examined as PW-2.

To substantiate his evidence, he has exhibited OPD Book marked as Ex.P.12 and X-ray Films marked as Ex.P.13 SCCH-5 and he has assessed permanent physical disability of 20% of right lower limb, which is 10% of whole body.

In cross-examination he has categorically admitted that, he has not treated the petitioner and petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and 3 simple injuries and there is no fracture, only there is dislocation of right hip joint.
PW-2 Doctor has given assessment of disability i.e., whole body disability from the lower limb at the rate of 10%.

Under such circumstances, considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also by relying on citation reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343 between Rajkumar V/s. Ajay Kumar, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at the rate of 6.5% i.e., 1/3rd disability is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.
SCCH-5 14

. Further medical department incharge at Government Hospital, Bengaluru is examined as PW-3 and he has exhibited authorization letter marked as Ex.P.14, case file is marked as Ex.P.15, copy of MLC Extract is marked as Ex.P.16 and X-ray Films are marked as Ex.P.17.
15.

As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 21 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.8, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 16.02.2002 and the alleged accident is occurred on 15.04.2023, accordingly relying on Ex.P.8 his age is considered about 22 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 18 is Naveen Kumar B.T vs Prakash Gowda K.S on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6871712/

On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is considered.

Further on perusal of Ex.P.6.
SCCH-5 the District Hospital, Tumkur has issued wound certificate, petitioner has sustained 3 simple injuries and 1 grievous injury.

So as per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, petitioner has sustained tenderness of hip, abrasion on left knee, abrasion in right knee and posterior dislocation of right hip,
which is grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Sriranganath K.L. for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and evidence of PW-1 to PW-3 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical expenses of Rs.1,583/-.
19.
Except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into SCCH-5 witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,61,710/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.201150020722800008500000 which is valid for the period from 29.06.2022 to 28.06.2025, the alleged accident was occurred on 15.04.2023 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Hence naturally liability of R1 shall go against R2, so SCCH-5 that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

23. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,61,710/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Sixty One Thousand Seven Hundred Ten Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,61,710/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Sixty One Thousand Seven Hundred Ten Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
